subject.title: fix(compaction): prevent repeated restarts after safety timeouts

question: Should OpenClaw accept one explicitly marked native compaction result produced immediately after wrapper-owned safety-timeout cancellation while the same reason’s bounded settlement token remains open?
rationale: The source can prove that the token is narrow and expires, but choosing whether any timeout-aborted work may mutate persisted session state requires explicit ownership intent.

options.title: Accept bounded timeout commits
options.body: Keep the exact-reason marked-result window, restore the shared helper, and land after exact-head checks prove late, external-abort, and unmarked results remain rejected.

options.title: Keep timeout fail-closed
options.body: Retain inner chunk partial-summary preservation and timeout guidance but remove the AgentSession post-timeout commit allowance.

options.title: Require full live proof
options.body: Pause until a realistic slow-provider or full gateway compaction run demonstrates forward progress without duplicate or late session-state writes.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded timeout commits
recommendation.body: Keep the exact-reason marked-result window, restore the shared helper, and land after exact-head checks prove late, external-abort, and unmarked results remain rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the assigned reviewer and the strongest recent history match for the compaction timeout boundary and helper lifecycle.
